title: A search for aggregate-level effects of education on fertility, using data from Zimbabwe
finding: NULL. District mean schooling and district literacy have no effect on a woman's birth rate beyond her own education, once urbanization is controlled.
adjudication_reason: The design is a direct test of the contextual/ideational claim: it asks whether community education moves fertility net of individual human capital. That is exactly the D.1.b estimand, and it is one of very few papers built to answer it. Confirmed in cell; the result is negative.

title: From Privilege to Prevalence: Contextual Effects of Women's Schooling on African Marital Timing
finding: Contextual effect present: the social meaning of a woman's schooling depends on her agemates' attainment, shifting marital timing beyond her own attainment. 30 countries.
adjudication_reason: Same contextual-versus-individual design logic as Kravdal, on a family-formation outcome rather than births. In cell, but the outcome level bars it from any fertility pool.

title: Shifting partnership ideals with online technologies among unmarried women in India
finding: Online-technology exposure associated with shifted partnership ideals among unmarried Indian women.
adjudication_reason: Treatment delivers family-model content (partnership ideals), which is the Wall-3 discriminator, so it stays. Outcome is a stated ideal, not a birth.

title: The Fall in Global Fertility: A Quantitative Model
finding: Calibrated structural model of global fertility decline; no empirical estimate of an ideational exposure.
adjudication_reason: This was the ONLY retrieved record in the value-added cell, and it is not an empirical design separating ideation from structure -- it is a quantitative model. The value-added cell is empty among retrieved records.

title: Population Control Policies and Fertility Convergence
finding: Reviews population-control policy and cross-country fertility convergence.
adjudication_reason: The operative variable is state population-control policy, not exposure to an external family model. Routes to A.5 (organized family planning programmes).

title: Does Electrification Spur the Fertility Transition? Evidence From Indonesia
finding: Electrification accounts for 18-24% of the fertility decline; TV exposure is a key channel, acting on preferences and contraceptive use; reduced child mortality is another pathway.
adjudication_reason: Wall 3 asks what the treatment delivers. Electrification delivers television ACCESS; the paper never establishes what content did the work, and it names contraceptive use (A.3) and child mortality (A.1) as co-equal pathways. This is channel geometry, not family-model content. Routes to A.20 with a cross-reference here.

title: Fertility, electricity and television: is there a link? Evidence from Pakistan, 1990-2018
finding: Associates electricity and television access with fertility decline in Pakistan.
adjudication_reason: Same Wall-3 defect as the Indonesia paper: infrastructural treatment, unspecified content.

title: A Cautionary Tale of Evaluating Identifying Assumptions: Did Reality TV Really Cause a Decline in Teenage Childbearing?
finding: Methodological critique of the Kearney-Levine reality-TV result on US teen births.
adjudication_reason: The setting is the United States, which is a source of the diffused package rather than a recipient, and the content is teen-pregnancy programming rather than a modern-family ideal. Fails the setting_era rule and Wall 3 together.

title: Competing Family Pathways for Immigrants and Their Descendants in Germany
finding: Compares partnership and fertility trajectories by origin group (Turkish, Russian, Kazak, Polish, Southern European), German SOEP.
adjudication_reason: The Wall-2 migrant seam: this is origin-norm persistence and differential trajectories, not convergence WITH exposure. Routes to A.19.

title: Does Female Schooling Reduce Fertility? Evidence from Nigeria
finding: Female schooling reduces fertility (IV, Universal Primary Education).
adjudication_reason: Enumerates three candidate channels in the introduction -- opportunity cost, contraceptive knowledge, female autonomy -- and tests none of them separately. Enumerating channels is not decomposing them. Stays unresolved.

title: The Impact of Education on Fertility and Child Mortality: Do Fathers Really Matter Less Than Mothers?
finding: Education affects fertility; compares maternal and paternal education.
adjudication_reason: Decomposes by WHOSE education, not by which mechanism. Stays unresolved.

title: Empowering Women Through Education: Evidence from Sierra Leone
finding: Schooling raised attainment and changed women's attitudes toward health practices and violence against women; no attitude effect for men.
adjudication_reason: The closest of the seven to an ideational reading, and still not a decomposition: the attitudes measured are about health and violence, not family-model ideals, and no fertility estimate is split by channel. Would route to D.2.a on its attitudinal content if it were being routed on that alone.

title: Fewer mothers with more colleges? The impacts of expansion in higher education on first marriage and first childbirth
finding: College expansion delays first marriage and first birth.
adjudication_reason: Explicitly separates a 'quantity effect' from a 'return effect' -- but both are economic. A decomposition between two economic channels does not resolve Wall 5, which asks whether the effect is ideational or economic at all.

title: The Impact of Education on Fertility During the Chinese Reform Era (1980-2018)
structural_controls_adjusted: birth cohort; fertility policy interaction; parity
finding: Education effects on fertility differ across parities and interact with fertility policy.
adjudication_reason: Frames explicitly on Caldwell's wealth flows alongside microeconomics and gender equity, then tests differential effects BY PARITY rather than by mechanism. Framing on Caldwell is not evidence for Caldwell.

title: The Causal Effects of Education on Age at Marriage and Marital Fertility
finding: Reviews Caldwell 1980's mass-schooling mechanisms explicitly; reports no evidence of a causal effect of education on lifetime fertility.
adjudication_reason: Cites Caldwell's mechanism by name and still does not separate it from opportunity cost. Also fails the setting rule: historical England is the source of the diffused package, not a case of it, so it routes to OFF_OTHER on setting even though its Wall-5 status is what was being checked.

title: Is Educating Girls the Best Investment for South Asia? Association Between Female Education and Fertility
finding: Negative association between female literacy and TFR in South Asia.
adjudication_reason: A narrative review of associations, not an estimate. evidence_type=review. Stays unresolved and is excluded from any pool on evidence type.

title: Exploring reproductive trajectories of youths of Oromia, Ethiopia: A life course approach
finding: Describes reproductive trajectories of Ethiopian youth.
adjudication_reason: Descriptive sequence analysis with no causal estimate and no mechanism decomposition.
